preamble: In Ucayali-Pajonal Ashéninka (Kampan, Peru) the alveolar tap /ɾ/ becomes the labio-velar glide /w/ between /a/ and /o/ in either order. It is the most frequent morphophonemic alternation in the language: the 3rd person feminine suffix -ro surfaces as -wo after a, and the medial enclitic =ra and absential =ranki surface as =wa and =wanki after the feminine prefix ro-. The rule is conditioned by the flanking vowels rather than by particular morphemes, but no parallel case outside Kampan has been found.

examples.note: The 3rd person feminine object suffix -ro becomes -wo after a.

examples.to: rowanki 'that (absent, feminine)', as in rowanki pankotsi 'that (absent) house'
examples.note: /ɾ/ > /w/ in /o_a/ position; the masculine counterpart riranki keeps the tap.

sources: Pedrós Caballero, T. (2023). A grammar of Ashéninka (Ucayali-Pajonal). LOT Dissertation Series 640. https://doi.org/10.48273/LOT0640
